prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: an attorney managing a parent's account. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a caller says they are acting under power of attorney or a similar authority, I should pause ordinary account discussion until I have checked the scope of that authority and whether it covers claims decisions as well as payments."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the attorney is managing a parent’s account, I should treat identity checks separately for the attorney and the policyholder, because the attorney can speak for the claim but does not automatically become the insured person."},{"type":"observation","content":"When documents are missing, I should ask early for the authority evidence, death paperwork if relevant, and any specific claim forms together, so the case does not stall in repeated chasers."},{"type":"preference","content":"When an attorney is anxious or unfamiliar with insurance processes, I should explain each step in plain English and avoid jargon, because a clear route through the claim reduces confusion and complaint risk."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the attorney reports the parent cannot manage the home or vehicle directly, I should check whether the claim needs extra safeguarding for vulnerable-customer handling and whether correspondence should be redirected."},{"type":"observation","content":"When there is a dispute between family members about who should act, I should not let the claim progress on verbal assurances alone; I should wait for the legal authority or a formal instruction from the recognised representative."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the attorney asks for repair or settlement decisions, I should confirm they understand the policyholder’s duties, excess, settlement method and any limits on delegated authority before I rely on their instructions."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the claim involves a home that the parent no longer visits, I should check occupation status, maintenance responsibilities and any unoccupied-property conditions early, because these can affect cover and triage."},{"type":"preference","content":"When an attorney provides documents, I should summarise what has been received and what is still needed in one message, because a single written checklist works better than scattered updates."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the attorney is only managing money but not the claim itself, I should restrict discussions to payment handling and keep claim assessment with the appropriate authorised contact, so delegated authority stays within bounds."}]}
